industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): financials and real estate investment trusts were the only sectors bought in the week (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct), Wood favours financials as the diversification from artificial intelligence, and Goldman (16 Oct) says Southern European banks are healthier than in 2011-15; against it, French spreads at decade highs with new spillover to Italy, the sovereign-bank loop. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, B prior. Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): risk-off cuts assets under management and flows (DNB Carnegie expect 'reduced trading velocity' at Avanza after 'recent turbulence in public markets', 14-Oct) while the cases are capital-light, cash-yielding and self-funded, which the regime pays for; EQT reported fee-generating assets ahead of consensus. Banca Mediolanum's memo (Mixed) finds the business congruent and the Italian multiple not. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: C now, B prior. Balanced; Neutral is a judgement. Counter-case for lower: a bear market compounds through performance and outflows; for higher: wealth managers are the simple yield cases investors crowd to.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with a stated entry level; medium conviction. Banca Mediolanum (BMED-IT) is a very good business at a full price: a 'Compounder' case whose modal return from 22.9 EUR (2026-10-09) is 9.3 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.2 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The case progresses at about 19.9 EUR on the eighteen-month path (about 13 percent below the reference price), or earlier on evidence that the recurring fee margin has stopped falling, which is the one development that would move the modal multiple toward the held branch. The park rule's four gates are all clear (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability A); the case is parked on the return against the bar, not on a gate. The adverse drop-through case (tax rate 26 percent, performance fees 100 million EUR a year) leaves the rating F and the recommendation unchanged, and lowers the clearing price to about 18.0 EUR.
case: - The case is a compounder, not a change: Italy's largest adviser network converts household cash into managed assets at a 70 percent rate on a fixed adviser base, and a 0.9-to-1.1-year government bond book turned the 2022 to 2026 rate cycle into a 30 percent rise in net interest income in H1 2026.

- The change the thesis rests on is small and already in the numbers. Two forces: the rate path (the 2026 net interest income guide lifted to +15 to +18 percent; a December 2026 ECB hike standing in the weekly environment reading of 2026-10-09; the company's 2027 plan needs only a 2.6 percent average Euribor) and the NEXT network programme (783 paired consultants in July 2026 from 590 at end-2025; paired seniors gather 28 percent more managed inflows; July and August 2026 the two best managed-inflow months in the company's history). The internal change fails the screen rule: no chief executive change, no acquisition, no buyback; only the guidance increase is strong. None of the framework's false-positive red flags fires.

- The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: from the choices (3 percent deposit campaigns, junior pairings) through the operating metrics (70 percent conversion, 783 consultants) and the financial statements (operating margin +20 percent) into the sell-side's estimates (consensus FY2026 EPS +21 percent in twelve months). What remains at the sell-side layer is a 3 to 6.5 percent gap between the record's path and the brokers' for FY2026 to FY2028, which is net interest income (the environment's rate path over the brokers' 2.6 percent Euribor glide) and the inflow run-rate (the July and August records over the H1 dip).
counter_case: - At the 'Investment Thesis' level, the strongest case against: H1 2026 is a rate-and-market peak dressed as structural growth, the risks research's "false friend" (asset gathering masks margin compression), the pre-mortem profile with the fewest hard inconsistencies. Net interest income's +30 percent came from a one-off funding relief (promotional deposits repriced from 4 and 5 percent to 3 percent) and the carry on a 0.9-year book at the top of the Euribor cycle, on a book with a 30 percent deposit beta against Fineco's 20 percent; the cost of funding is already rising again (0.69 percent in Q1 2026 to 0.84 percent in Q2 2026). The recurring fee margin is in structural decline (214 to 198 basis points), with Grandi Patrimoni, the growth segment, pricing down to 1 percent and automatic-strategy inflows diluting it further. Adviser costs are at 36 percent of gross commissions and rising, with the recruitment market tightening (Intesa's 6,300 hires; Banca Generali's recruitment inflows +43 percent). Performance fees of 256 million EUR in 2025 are a bull-market record on 80 percent of products. FY2025's reported growth was a 13.4 percent tax rate on a pre-tax profit that fell 1.4 percent. The brokers, who see all this, have FY2027 EPS at +2 percent and three of the last four notes at Hold. Add the environment: Italy named the next sovereign after France, the Banks row off Overweight, the stock above its ten-year 'mania' band. On this reading earnings are flat to down from FY2026 and the multiple reverts to 11.4x: 11.4 x 1.69 EUR of consensus FY2028 earnings is 19.3 EUR, plus 1.41 EUR of dividends, 20.7 EUR against 22.9 EUR, a loss of about 10 percent over eighteen months; Jefferies' bear target of 17.00 EUR sits inside that.

- What the record concedes: every number is in the research and the record has used most of them against the case itself; the fee margin is falling and the research gives no reason it stops; the adviser-cost line is a structural transfer from shareholders to the network; the tax base is flattered; the multiple is at the top; the growth is single-digit.
triggers: - Progress trigger: a price of about 19.9 EUR on the eighteen-month modal path (17.3 EUR on the three-year path; 21.4 EUR with the multiple held; about 18.0 EUR in the adverse drop-through case); or, earlier, a quarter in which the recurring fee margin stops falling, the one development that would move the modal multiple toward the held branch; or a cohort-wide re-rating led by Banca Generali and Azimut.

- Euribor and net interest income: Alarm at three-month Euribor below 2.25 percent; Invalidate at Euribor futures below 2 percent (the risks research's re-run trigger and the Industry Digest's common invalidation across financials), or two quarters of net interest income below 240 million EUR with rates unchanged; confirm above 240 million EUR a quarter with rates holding.

- Managed-inflow conversion: confirm above 750 million EUR a month (the 9 billion EUR run-rate); Alarm at a month below 600 million EUR managed; Invalidate below 1.5 billion EUR a quarter for two quarters, or conversion below 65 percent on a maturing campaign.
- Recurring fee margin: Alarm at compression of 5 basis points in a quarter; Invalidate below 190 basis points.
- The multiple: Alarm at an Italian sovereign-spread episode with Italy above 150 basis points; no measured Invalidate level, a judgement.
- Inducement ban: Alarm at a concrete Commission proposal to ban or cap inducements.
